accessibility: Check semantics, labels, contrast, keyboard access, and focus before sharing.
accessibility-decisions: Record accessibility decisions and trade-offs, with handoff criteria engineering can build to.
adaptive-interfaces: Spec how a screen responds to reduced motion, contrast, text size, and density preferences.
assumption-mapper: Separate what the team knows from what it assumes before research or building begins.
audit: Check a prototype’s design system, accessibility, and copy before sharing.
benchmark: Score your own flow against best-in-class examples and name the gaps worth closing.
case-study: Write a project case study from its brief, findings, and decisions, with every claim sourced.
cognitive-accessibility: Check mental load, wayfinding, memory demands, and decision complexity, beyond contrast and ARIA.
competitor-scan: Find how one competitor handles a specific feature or flow.
conceptual-model: Define the product’s objects, relationships, states, and vocabulary before drawing screens.
docs-brief: Draft a short status or decision brief as a page in Confluence, Notion, or Google Docs.
content: Write and review interface copy against your product’s voice and terminology.
critique-prep: Write a presenter script for a design critique: framing, walk order, and the feedback you want.
decision-first-research: Turn a research request into a clear decision, the evidence it needs, and the smallest useful study.
deck-builder: Turn finished findings into a presentation deck, using only evidence from the project.
design-debt-tracker: Standalone triage and review of the per-project design debt register (projects/<slug>/debt.md).
design-handoff: Capture layout, components, states, and edge cases in a draft engineering spec.
design-kickoff: Turn a new request into a researched brief, with an approval step before building.
design-memory: Keep a private record of how you tend to design across projects.
design-rationale: Record the options, evidence, and tradeoffs behind a design decision.
design-retrospective: Reflect on a shipped project: what worked, what didn’t, and what to carry forward.
design-system: Check whether a style value already exists as a token before anything is written.
designer-workload: Older version of workload-agent, kept for compatibility. Use workload-agent instead.
diagnostic: Find the design bottleneck and decide which workflow to run next.
figma-asset-sync: Download icons and images from Figma and package them for code.
figma-code-sync: Map Figma components to their code counterparts using Code Connect.
figma-effects-catalog: Document the custom shader effects and fills used in your Figma files.
figma-library-manager: Find existing library components before creating new ones in Figma.
figma-token-sync: Find drift between Figma variables and your code tokens, and sync them in either direction.
figma-ux-audit: Audit a Figma page and place colour-coded annotation cards next to each screen.
harness-setup: Bring in your design system, brand guidelines, and company context, or start from the examples.
ia-methods: Plan and analyze card sorts and tree tests to check your information architecture.
icon-usage: Use icons from your icon library through one component, never hand-drawn SVG.
insight-writer: Turn research patterns into insights that explain why they matter and what to do next.
inspiration-scouting: Collect visual and interaction references, with what to take and what to leave from each.
interaction-design: Specify component states and feedback across keyboard, touch, and screen readers.
interface-change-review: Review only the UI you changed, and separate new issues from regressions and old ones.
live-page-review: Capture a live page and route its evidence into the right review workflow.
manager-1on1-prep: Prepare a 1:1 with a direct report from their live work and recent updates.
mobile-shell: Keep phone-frame prototypes consistent: status bar, navigation, tab bar, and sheets.
motion-choreography: Spec, review, and plan purposeful animation, always with a reduced-motion alternative.
okr-goal-setting: Define a measurable design goal connected to a real business outcome.
org-pack-builder: Gather your company context, vocabulary, voice, and patterns into files your agent can read.
people-coaching: Prepare feedback, a difficult conversation, or a growth plan for someone you manage.
presenter: Choose how to show built screens to a reviewer, then set up that view.
product-strategy: Connect user opportunities to business outcomes and solution bets with an opportunity solution tree.
publish-project: Publish a project’s share pages to a public link when you choose to.
research-agent: Gather existing product knowledge and source evidence for a new design task.
research-artifacts: Build personas, journey maps, job stories, and service blueprints from real research.
research-question-sharpener: Rewrite vague research questions so they produce usable answers, and flag the ones research can’t answer.
research-shareout: Plan how to share research so stakeholders engage and act on it.
research-summary: Summarize a research session or study so the team can see the findings and next steps.
research-synthesis: Turn interview notes and transcripts into tagged evidence and pattern candidates.
responsive-patterns: Content-driven breakpoint strategy, reflow, priority shifting, and 200% zoom / WCAG 1.4.10 discipline for multi-width layouts.
review-report: Turn a finished design critique into a readable HTML report.
roadmap-prioritization: Rank design work using evidence, business goals, and an explicit effort appetite.
scheduling: Find a meeting slot and draft the invite with real context from the project.
screener-builder: Write a recruitment screener that selects participants by behaviour, not demographics.
session-handoff: Save the decisions and open questions so the next agent session can continue.
stakeholder-alignment: Identify who needs to agree, what matters to them, and the decision to ask for.
synthetic-user-testing: Walk a prototype through key tasks as named personas to find friction before real testing.
taste-feedback: Check visual density, weight, and hierarchy mid-build, before a full critique.
ticket-create: Draft a ticket and file it in Jira, Linear, or GitHub Issues once you say go.
ui-agent: Build a screen using your product’s design tokens and shared components.
usability-test-guide: Prepare the tasks, questions, and measures for a usability test.
ux-review: Run a five-persona UX review on a URL, HTML file, screenshot, or Figma frame and get one scored report.
ux-pattern: Review a flow’s structure against how your product works, not just how it looks.
workload-agent: Check the live product roadmap and design workload from connected boards.
workshop-whiteboard: Run a timed research-scoping board with your team, from problem to plan.
writing: Write long-form pieces such as articles, essays, and case-study write-ups, with every claim sourced.
